articles.title: NASA’s ESCAPADE Completes Powered Earth Flybys, Now En Route to Mars
articles.description: NASA’s two ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) spacecraft have each successfully completed a powered Earth flyby, using Earth’s gravity in combination with a sustained engine burn to slingshot themselves toward Mars. With these successful maneuvers complete, the twin spacecraft are on target to reach the Red Planet in September 2027. “This is […]
articles.summary: NASA's ESCAPADE spacecraft successfully completed powered Earth flybys and are now en route to Mars for groundbreaking plasma studies. This dual-mission represents a major scientific milestone in understanding planetary atmospheres.

articles.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
articles.description: NASA has revealed an accelerated plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing competing lunar landers and a crucial orbital test scheduled for 2027. Faster rocket preparations, new lightweight spacesuits, and redesigned missions could help pave the way for a permanent lunar presence and future human exploration of Mars.
articles.summary: NASA announces an accelerated lunar return mission for 2028 with SpaceX and Blue Origin, marking a major milestone in returning humans to the Moon.

articles.title: SpaceX will launch epic double-catch Starship Flight 15 test mission on Nov. 13
articles.description: SpaceX's next Starship test flight will take place on Friday (Nov. 13), and it will be epic: The company will try to catch both of the vehicle's stages when they return to Earth.
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 will attempt an unprecedented double-catch maneuver, using the launch tower's mechanical arms to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage. This audacious test represents a major milestone in reusable rocket technology.

articles.title: NASA unveils $10B Moon base contract as SpaceX, Blue Origin join lunar gold rush
articles.description: NASA announced Saturday that Elon Musk’s SpaceX, Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin and six other aerospace companies are eligible to compete for up to $10 billion in lunar delivery contracts as the agency advances plans to establish a permanent base on the moon. The an…
articles.summary: NASA awards a $10 billion Moon base contract to SpaceX, Blue Origin, and six other aerospace companies, marking a major milestone in humanity's return to the lunar surface. This public-private partnership accelerates the development of sustainable lunar infrastructure.

articles.title: La NASA busca a la próxima generación de astronautas
articles.description: Read this release in English here.La NASA busca a los exploradores que ayudarán a escribir el próximo capítulo de los vuelos espaciales tripulados. Ya está abierto el plazo de inscripción para la próxima promoción de astronautas de la agencia, que se incorporarán a la NASA en un momento en el que Estados Unidos regresa a […]
articles.summary: NASA opens recruitment for the next generation of astronauts to lead humanity's future exploration missions. This call represents a pivotal moment in expanding the diversity and talent pool of space explorers.

articles.title: NASA’s Chandra Finds Source of Star’s Mysterious Outbursts
articles.description: Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what is triggering repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star. A new study, published Monday in the latest issue of The Astrophysical Journal, details the discovery of a previously hidden companion object that keeps pulling material away from the massive star every 113 days as they orbit […]
articles.summary: NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory has identified the mechanism triggering mysterious outbursts from a giant star. This discovery deepens our understanding of stellar behavior and extreme cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: La NASA destina un millón de dólares al reto estudiantil Base Lunar
articles.description: Read this release in English here.El domingo 8 de noviembre de 2026, la NASA anunció la convocatoria del reto estudiantil Base Lunar, dotado con un millón de dólares, durante un acto de MAX POWER celebrado en el Complejo de Visitantes del Centro Espacial Kennedy, en Florida. En el marco de una edad de oro de […]
articles.summary: NASA awards one million dollars to a student lunar base challenge, inspiring the next generation of engineers and scientists. This program fosters innovation and hands-on experience in lunar exploration technology.

articles.title: MAX POWER: NASA’s Inaugural Aerospace Expo Ignites America’s Future
articles.description: Thousands gathered over several days in early November to experience MAX POWER – NASA’s first exhibition of America’s superiority in space, aeronautics, and technology on and around the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The multi-day, family-friendly event honored the nation’s 250th anniversary and served as a culmination of the agency’s Inspiration Tour. Among the […]
articles.summary: NASA's inaugural MAX POWER aerospace exhibition showcased America's aerospace innovations to thousands of visitors. The event inspired public enthusiasm for space exploration and technological advancement.

articles.title: CHAPEA Mission 2 Crew Reflects After 378 Days on Simulated Mars
articles.description: After 378 days without windows, the sounds of the outside world, or real-time calls with family and friends, four research volunteers stepped out of NASA’s Mars Dune Alpha habitat on Oct. 31, completing the agency’s second yearlong Mars surface simulation.  Ross Elder, Ellen Ellis, James Spicer, and Matthew Montgomery entered the roughly 1,700-square-foot, 3D-printed habitat at […]
articles.summary: Four researchers completed 378 days in CHAPEA's simulated Mars habitat, providing invaluable data for human Mars preparation. This landmark analog mission advances our readiness for long-duration space exploration.

articles.title: A Stellar Odd Couple at an Unusual Stage of Evolution
articles.description: Millisecond pulsars are fascinating objects that serve as natural clocks in the Universe. They form by drawing material and angular momentum from a companion. This mass transfer can rapidly accelerate the companion's evolution to a white dwarf. Astronomers have detected a millisecond pulsar's white dwarf companion that appears to be observed just as the mass transfer completed. They can still see some of the debris.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered a fascinating binary system of a millisecond pulsar at an unusual evolutionary stage. This rare stellar pairing provides new insights into stellar dynamics and compact object formation.

articles.title: Nearby Dwarf Galaxies Show Surprising Lack Of Oxygen, Says Paper
articles.description: A new study of more than three dozen dwarf galaxies has surprised researchers with just how little oxygen they have been able to retain over cosmic time.  The results reveal that we still have major gaps in our understanding of galaxy evolution.
articles.summary: A comprehensive study of dwarf galaxies reveals surprising oxygen scarcity, challenging previous understanding of galactic chemical evolution. This finding opens new questions about star formation and elemental distribution in the universe.

articles.title: Our Sun’s Undiscovered Stellar Nemesis Is Still Out There, Says Physicist
articles.description: The decades old idea that our solar system’s Oort Cloud is continually perturbed by a heretofore undetected low mass Red Dwarf star remains the best explanation for periodicities found in Earth’s impact record.  Or so says a well known physicist who has long championed this idea.
articles.summary: A physicist presents compelling evidence that our solar system's Oort Cloud may be perturbed by an undiscovered low-mass companion star. This hypothesis could reshape our understanding of our cosmic neighborhood.

articles.title: The ELT Can Probe Ultra-Diffuse Galaxies and Their Dark Matter Mysteries
articles.description: Ultra-Diffuse Galaxies are strange because they're as large as the Milky Way, but have far fewer stars. It's as if they're puffed up for some reason. Determining what's going on with them could help confirm the Lambda-CDM model. A new proposed instrument for the Extremely Large Telescope could give astronomers their best look yet at these strange galaxies.
articles.summary: The Extremely Large Telescope will enable unprecedented study of ultra-diffuse galaxies and their dark matter composition. This capability promises to solve one of cosmology's most intriguing mysteries about galaxies larger than the Milky Way.

articles.title: NASA's Twin Spacecraft Will Execute Powered Slingshot Maneuvers on Their Way to Mars
articles.description: NASA's ESCAPADE mission features a pair of identical spacecraft on their way to Mars. They launched outside of the normal launch window, so they'll perform powered slingshot maneuvers to boost their speed. Once there, they'll "fly" in formation and study how the solar wind interacts with what remains of Mars ancient magnetosphere.
articles.summary: NASA's ESCAPADE mission features twin spacecraft executing powered slingshot maneuvers en route to Mars, advancing our understanding of the Red Planet's atmosphere and space environment.

articles.title: JWST tracks more than 100 magnified stellar events in the Dragon galaxy
articles.description: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), a team of astronomers identified 104 magnified stellar events in a galaxy known as the Dragon, located around 6.5 billion light-years away. This discovery more than doubles the previous record of 44 such detections in the same galaxy. Because these kinds of events reveal some of the most luminous stars and likely the presence of dark matter, this study offers a rare look at the galaxy's stellar population along with a possible hint at the nature of dark matter.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has identified 104 magnified stellar events in the Dragon galaxy, revealing previously hidden cosmic phenomena through gravitational lensing.

articles.title: Want to fly to the moon? NASA is looking for new astronauts to help grow its Artemis program
articles.description: Want to fly to the moon and help build a permanent lunar base? NASA is accepting applications for a new astronaut class that will help grow the Artemis program.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA is recruiting a new astronaut class to support the Artemis program's ambitious goal of establishing a permanent human presence on the Moon.

articles.title: Caltech robot makes history by building a structure in space
articles.description: For the first time, a robot has autonomously built part of a structure in space, demonstrating a breakthrough that could fundamentally change space exploration. The technology could one day allow scientists to construct enormous telescopes, communications antennas, and solar power stations in orbit, far beyond the size limits of today's rockets.
articles.summary: A Caltech robot has autonomously constructed a structure in space for the first time, demonstrating breakthrough technology for future construction in orbital and extraplanetary environments.

articles.title: Mysterious gas leaks suggest Mars may still be volcanically alive
articles.description: Mysterious gas emissions and fresh volcanic fissures suggest that Mars may not be geologically dead after all, with hot magma potentially still active deep underground. The discovery could point to hidden pockets of warmth and chemical energy capable of supporting microbial life beneath the Red Planet’s surface.
articles.summary: Mysterious gas emissions and fresh volcanic features suggest that Mars may retain active geothermal activity, transforming our understanding of the planet's geology.

articles.title: Einstein's equations reveal how gravity could break, reconnect, and release energy
articles.description: More than a century after Einstein revolutionized our understanding of gravity, scientists have uncovered a surprising new phenomenon hidden within his equations. Researchers at Columbia University and Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez have identified a theoretical process called "gravitational reconnection," in which structures within gravitational fields can break apart and reconnect, transferring energy into matter.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered new insights into Einstein's gravitational equations, revealing mechanisms for how gravity could break and reconnect while releasing energy. This breakthrough deepens our century-long understanding of gravity's fundamental nature.

articles.title: NASA is racing against time to save the Hubble Space Telescope
articles.description: NASA is exploring a daring plan to save the legendary Hubble Space Telescope from its eventual fiery plunge into Earth's atmosphere. After more than 35 years of groundbreaking discoveries, Hubble is slowly losing altitude, and without intervention, it could fall back to Earth as early as 2033 or 2034. To keep the iconic observatory operating, NASA is asking private space companies to propose innovative ways to boost Hubble into a higher orbit, upgrade its capabilities, or safely dispose of it when its mission finally ends.
articles.summary: NASA is developing an innovative plan to extend the operational life of the Hubble Space Telescope and prevent its deorbiting. This daring rescue mission would preserve one of humanity's most transformative scientific instruments.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists have found evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay after a 42-year search, marking a significant breakthrough in understanding exotic particles and fundamental physics. This discovery opens new windows into the subatomic realm.

articles.title: Step inside the zeptoverse: British scientists use the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside a minuscule world where exotic particles may be hiding
articles.description: British scientists have used the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside the minuscule world of the zeptoverse.
articles.summary: British scientists using the Large Hadron Collider have peered into the zeptoverse, exploring the minuscule quantum world where exotic particles may exist. This research pushes the boundaries of particle physics and our understanding of reality's smallest scales.

articles.title: Nanohertz Gravitational-Wave Constraints on Supermassive Binary Black Holes at Cosmic Dawn
articles.description: Author(s): Yiqin Chen, Shi-Yi Zhao, Xingjiang Zhu, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Małgorzata Curyło, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Wenhua Ling, Rami F. Mandow, Richard N. Manchester, Saurav Mishra, Daniel J. Reardon, Sparrow Roch, Christopher…
articles.summary: Researchers use nanohertz gravitational-wave observations to constrain the properties of supermassive binary black holes in the early universe. This work advances our understanding of black hole formation and evolution at cosmic dawn.

articles.title: Two Different Kinds of Gamma-Ray Bursts Erupted 4 Minutes Apart. Astronomers Have Never Seen This Before.
articles.description: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most energetic cosmic events since the Big Bang, releasing the most energetic type of radiation, gamma rays – the stuff that turned unassuming Bruce Banner into the rampaging Hulk, but on an astronomical, potentially plan…
articles.summary: Astronomers observed two distinct types of gamma-ray bursts erupting just 4 minutes apart, an unprecedented occurrence that challenges existing models of these energetic cosmic explosions. This rare event provides new insights into the most violent phenomena in the universe.

articles.title: NASA Awards Moon Base Transportation, Technology, Science Projects
articles.description: NASA announced a suite of awards and mission updates on Saturday to expand the agency’s Moon Base exploration, science, and infrastructure capabilities. The investments will advance commercial robotic deliveries, a nuclear-powered rover named PROMISE, launch …
articles.summary: NASA announces major awards and mission updates for expanded Moon Base exploration, science, and technology development initiatives. These investments strengthen humanity's capability for sustainable lunar operations.

articles.title: Pour protéger la Terre, la sonde Hera a rejoint un astéroïde frappé par la Nasa !
articles.description: La sonde Hera de l’ESA, après un voyage de deux ans vers un système d’astéroïdes situé actuellement à 196,8 millions de kilomètres de la Terre, a livré ses premières images à leur sujet. L'un de ses principaux objectifs est de mieux les comprendre afin de nou…
articles.summary: The ESA's Hera probe successfully reached an asteroid system previously impacted by NASA's planetary defense mission. This follow-up investigation validates asteroid deflection techniques and advances planetary protection science.

articles.title: NASA Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket Challenge
articles.description: Mid-power (3-7 kW) Hall effect thruster systems have been identified by government and industry stakeholders as critical capabilities for satellite, defense, and exploration missions. Given the need for this capability, NASA is launching the Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket (AMPERE) Challenge. The NASA AMPERE Challenge invites U.S. commercial companies to develop and demonstrate mid-power Hall effect […]
articles.summary: NASA's Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket Challenge advances Hall effect thruster technology for next-generation propulsion systems. This initiative drives innovation in efficient, sustainable space exploration technology.

articles.title: Astronauts Across Generations Share the Stage
articles.description: On Nov. 6, 2026, Purpose Entertainment hosted the Artemis Celebration Gala at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida. Held on the eve of NASA’s MAX POWER event, the gala celebrated the explorers, innovators, and visionaries advancing the next era of human spaceflight. The event honored the successful completion of the agency’s […]
articles.summary: Astronauts from multiple generations gathered at NASA's Kennedy Space Center for the Artemis Celebration Gala. This event highlighted the continuity of human spaceflight achievement and intergenerational inspiration.

articles.title: A Perseverance Experiment Could Help Astronauts Prepare for Dust Storms on Mars
articles.description: Researchers at Washington University examined how dust interacts with the spacesuit swatches on the Perseverance Rover. Future missions to Mars require that planners account for the effects of dust exposure on humans and materials.
articles.summary: Perseverance Rover experiments are helping scientists understand how Martian dust affects spacesuits, crucial for astronaut safety. This research directly supports future human exploration of Mars.

articles.title: An Artificial CORTEX to Guide Satellite Rescue Missions
articles.description: Thousands of so-called zombie satellites orbit Earth in the critical Low-Earth Orbit regime. They're either inactive or have stopped alerting other satellites to their presence. Researchers are building a system called CORTEX that can guide a repair satellite to autonomously dock with these zombies.
articles.summary: An artificial intelligence system called CORTEX is being developed to guide satellite rescue and debris removal missions. This innovation promises to protect critical orbital infrastructure and enable sustainable space operations.
